children: Shares of IT distribution giant TD SYNNEX
fell 8.9% in the pre-market session after the company reported its Q3 CY2026 financial results.

According to a company press release, TD SYNNEX reported quarterly revenue of $21.6 billion, representing a 37.7% increase year over year and surpassing the high end of its financial outlook. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was $5.68, reflecting a 58.7% increase compared to the previous year, and non-GAAP operating income expanded 55.1% year over year to $736 million. TD SYNNEX returned $139 million to stockholders through approximately $100 million in share repurchases and $38 million in dividend payments, while declaring a quarterly cash dividend of $0.48 per common share.

However, the underlying results showed margin compression and cash strain, according to the release. Gross margin contracted 61 basis points to 6.61%, and free cash flow dropped to negative $975.6 million from positive $213.9 million a year ago as inventories reached $15.3 billion. On a more positive note, CEO Patrick Zammit said Distribution and Hyve both exceeded expectations on enterprise artificial intelligence adoption and data center modernization. Looking ahead, TD SYNNEX forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $21.8 billion to $22.6 billion and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $5.65 to $6.15, the release revealed.Fulfilling hyperscale artificial intelligence orders drives volume rapidly, but it compresses gross margin and ties up substantial working capital. With free cash flow turning sharply negative to fund server inventory, investors are likely weighing the capital cost required to deliver that top-line growth.
What Is The Market Telling Us

TD SYNNEX’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 8 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 6 months ago when the stock gained 8% on the news that investor sentiment turned positive on hopes of a potential ceasefire in Iran, which also contributed to easing oil prices.

Wall Street started the new quarter with a tech-led rally, as major indices like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite posted significant gains. The optimism stemmed from news of potential de-escalation in geopolitical tensions, which often encourages a 'risk-on' environment. In such a climate, investors are more willing to move capital into growth-oriented assets, such as technology stocks, which powered the market's upward move. The broad-based gains across sectors indicated a decisive shift in market sentiment, away from the caution that had prevailed previously.

TD SYNNEX is up 70.4% since the beginning of the year, but at $261.36 per share, it is still trading 9.9% below its 52-week high of $290.14 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of TD SYNNEX’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,346.
